source.notes: This is a SPECIMEN paper published by CISCE for the ISC 2027 examination (examYear 2027); found on https://cisce.org/specimen-question-papers-isc-class-xii-2027/. The PDF has 20 pages: pages 1-13 are the question paper (13 printed pages) and pages 14-20 are the Answer Key for the same paper, so answerSourceUrl equals sourceUrl and answerSourceFile is null. Cover page states Maximum Marks 70, Time Allotted Three Hours plus an additional fifteen minutes reading time (not included in durationMinutes=180, which is the writing time only). Section A is one Question 1 with eighteen roman-numeral subparts (i)-(xviii); subparts (xvi) and (xviii) each contain two further lettered (a)/(b) subparts, each printed with its own [1] mark, so Section A is stored as 20 separate one-mark entries (number '1', part '(i)' ... '(xviii)(b)') totalling the printed 20 marks for the section. Sections B, C and D each have questions offering an internal choice marked 'OR' between two whole alternatives (e.g. Question 6 (i) OR (ii)); each alternative is stored as its own entry sharing choiceGroup = the question number, with any lettered sub-parts inside that alternative kept together in one entry's text because they are not printed with individual marks. Where a question has multiple sub-parts but no internal 'OR' and no individually printed marks (e.g. Questions 3, 4, 7, 11), the sub-parts are kept together in a single entry for that question number. cognitiveLevel is recorded only where a single Bloom's-style tag (e.g. '(Recall)', '(Analyse)') is printed for the whole stored entry; where a combined entry's sub-parts carry different printed tags, cognitiveLevel is omitted rather than guessed. Several questions reference a pie chart, Venn diagram, bar graph, flowchart, pedigree chart, nucleotide diagram or hand-drawn graph that is not reproduced by text extraction; each such question is flagged with hasFigure/extractionIssues. The filename code '863A' does not appear anywhere in the extracted document text, so paperCode was left null rather than guessed from the filename. The table in Question 17(ii)(b) (fruits X/Y/Z) extracted with an apparent row misalignment versus the official answer (the description that matches Fruit X in the answer key appears on the 'Y' row, and the 'X' row is blank); this is flagged rather than silently corrected. Stacked fractions in a few official answers (Question 12(ii), Question 18(ii)(a)) were linearised with '/' or rebuilt inline; each is flagged with a notation-rebuilt issue and MEDIUM confidence.

questions.text:
The image shown below represents an ecological hypothesis proposed by Paul Ehrlich. Study it carefully and answer the following question.
Identify and explain this ecological hypothesis.

officialAnswer.text:
Rivet Popper Hypothesis
Explanation:
• In an airplane (ecosystem), all parts are joined together using thousands of rivets (species)
• If the passengers travelling in it start popping a rivet (causing species to become extinct), it may not affect flight safety (proper functioning of the ecosystem) initially but as more and more rivets are removed, the plane becomes weak over a period.
• If rivets from wings are removed (important species), the flight safety (ecosystem) is affected immediately.

figures.alt: Two pictures side by side: a complete aeroplane and an aeroplane with its parts coming apart

questions.text:
The given pie chart shows the distribution of genotypes in a population of 9000 pea plants.
The population is in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium. It is known that 360 plants are homozygous recessive (tt).
Using this information, calculate the following:
(a) Frequency of the dominant allele (T)
(b) Number of heterozygous pea plants
extractionIssues: Pie chart (a graph/diagram of genotype distribution) on page 7 not reproduced in text layer; the values needed for the calculation (9000 plants, 360 homozygous recessive) are given in the text

officialAnswer.text:

(b) The number of heterozygous pea plants = 2pq = 0.32 of 9000 = 2880

questions.text:
A gene normally transcribes an mRNA of 603 nucleotides, including the stop codon, which encodes a functional protein. However, during DNA replication the 150th nucleotide was deleted.
(a) Predict how many amino acids will remain unchanged before the mutation site.
(b) Explain how the mutation is likely to affect the resulting protein.

officialAnswer.text:
(a) First 49 amino acids will remain unchanged.
(b) 50th amino acid and all subsequent amino acids are likely to be altered due to frame shift mutation.

questions.text:
A biotechnologist successfully inserts a gene for drought tolerance into isolated somatic cells of a wheat plant. She now needs to regenerate thousands of genetically identical, pathogen-free complete plants from these modified cells.
(a) Which technique should the biotechnologist use to develop these genetically modified cells of wheat into a complete plant?
(b) Explain two major steps involved in this technique.

officialAnswer.text:
(a) Micropropagation / Plant tissue culture
(b) Major steps:
• Explant is transferred to the culture medium under aseptic conditions.
• Auxin and cytokinin induce callus formation / differentiation.

questions.text:
The bar graph given below shows the growth of E. coli in two different media (Medium – A and Medium – B), along with the corresponding β-galactosidase activity and the state of the lac operon in each case.
Based on the above graph, answer the following questions:
(a) Why is the operon switched OFF in one medium?
(b) The lac operon is described as an example of negative regulation of gene expression. Explain the statement with reference to the role of the operator site.

officialAnswer.text:
(a) In the Medium A, only glucose is present and the inducer (lactose) is absent, so the repressor protein remains bound to the operator site, blocking RNA polymerase. Thus, the operon is switched OFF.
(b) In the Medium B, only lactose is present. It stops the repressor protein from binding to the operator site, allowing RNA polymerase to transcribe the structural genes. The operon gets switched ON.

figures.alt: Bar graph titled beta-galactosidase activity in two media, with bars for Medium A and Medium B labelled with their values

questions.text:
pBR322 was used in the making of genetically engineered insulin. What was the possible role played by this plasmid?
Can this plasmid be used for gene transfer in plants? Substantiate your opinion with a reason.

officialAnswer.text:
(i) Plasmid acted as a suitable vector.
(ii) No
Reason: It lacks the T-DNA / vir gene system necessary for transferring DNA into plant cells.

questions.text:
The following graph shows seasonal variations in Net Primary Productivity at the level of the surface and 1m depth in a marshy area of India during a study.
(i) Account for the difference in primary productivity at points ‘X’ and ‘Y’.
(ii) The GPP of a terrestrial ecosystem is 2700 kg/m²/yr and 3/10th of its energy is used for respiration. Calculate the amount of energy available as NPP.
extractionIssues: Official answer's stacked fraction 3 over 10 (followed by x 2700) written inline as (3/10) x 2700, as printed.

officialAnswer.text:
(i) Primary productivity decreases with decrease in temperature.
(ii) R = (3/10) x 2700 = 810 kg/m²/yr
NPP = GPP – R
NPP = 2700 – 810
NPP = 1890 kg/m²/ yr

figures.alt: Line graph titled Primary productivity in different months: NPP (mg/m3/hr) against months November to September, solid line for Surface and dashed line for 1m depth, with points marked X, Y and Z

questions.text: Describe three types of natural selection, illustrating each with a suitable graph.
extractionIssues: The marking scheme's illustrative graphs for each type of natural selection are not reproduced in text layer; only the textual descriptions were captured

officialAnswer.text:
Types of natural selection
• Stabilising - More individuals acquire mean character value.
• Directional - More individuals acquire value other than the mean character value.
• Disruptive - More individuals acquire peripheral character value at both ends of the distribution curve.

questions.text:
During an experiment, Sneha was given the following base sequence of mRNA of E. coli and asked to derive an amino acid sequence from it.
5′ GUG GCU CAA 3′
• She successfully derived the amino acid sequence as valine, alanine and glycine.
• Then, she was given the amino acid sequence of arginine, serine, proline and was asked to derive the base sequence of mRNA from it.
(i) Sneha could not derive the mRNA sequence successfully. Provide a scientific reason to explain why she could not determine it.
(ii) Later, she observed that GCU codon changed to GCA and the amino acid was alanine in the fungal cell. Which feature of genetic code enabled it?
(iii) Based on the sequence provided above, deduce the anticodon sequence of the tRNA and write it in the 5′ → 3′ orientation.

officialAnswer.text:
(i) Due to degeneracy of codon, because one amino acid is coded by more than one codon.
(ii) Genetic code is universal.
(iii) Anticodon sequence 5′ UUG AGC CAC 3′

questions.text:

The table below presents some features of proteins ‘X’ and ‘Y’. Study it and answer the following questions:
Features | Protein X | Protein Y
Patient suffering from the disease | Typhoid | Chikungunya
Mode of action | Slow but long lasting | Rapid but temporary
Effective against cancer cells | No | Yes
(i) Identify the proteins ‘X’ and ‘Y’.
(ii) How does protein ‘Y’ develop an immunological response in the patient suffering from Chikungunya?
extractionIssues: Table (features of proteins X and Y) flattened from a table layout in the PDF

questions.text:
(i) Marfan Syndrome is a human genetic disorder caused by a mutation in the FBN1 gene. This gene codes for fibrillin – 1, a protein that gives connective tissues strength and flexibility. People suffering from Marfan Syndrome show symptoms like dislocation of the eye lens, flat feet, unusually tall height and rupturing of aorta.
The following pedigree chart represents the pattern of inheritance of Marfan Syndrome in a family.
(a) Identify the type of inheritance from the given pedigree chart.
(b) If the parents of a child are heterozygous for this particular trait, calculate the probability of the child being unaffected using a Punnett square.
(ii) Prisha is provided with two nucleotides as shown below. Which of these nucleotides should she choose to make an ideal genetic material? Give a reason.
extractionIssues: Pedigree chart (Marfan Syndrome inheritance, Generations I-III) on page 11 not fully reproduced in text layer; only generation/individual numbering was captured, the family-tree connecting lines are lost

officialAnswer.text:
(i)(a) Autosomal dominant
(i)(b) Probability of unaffected child = 25%
(ii) Prisha should choose Nucleotide (2).
• The 2–OH group present in the nucleotide (1) is a reactive group. It will make the genetic material unstable and easily degradable.
• Nucleotide (2) is non-reactive.

figures.alt: Pedigree chart of three generations (I, II, III) with numbered circles and squares, some shaded

Two nucleotide structures labelled (1) and (2), each a five-carbon sugar ring with carbons numbered 1 to 5, a circle joined by CH2 at carbon 5, a box marked NITROGENOUS BASE ((A) in 1, (G) in 2) at carbon 1, and a group drawn below carbon 2

questions.text:
(a) Differentiate between the following based on the parameter specified below:
(1) Leydig cells and Sertoli cells based on Location in testis
(2) Corpus luteum and Placenta based on Endocrine function
(b) What would happen if the zona pellucida disappears prematurely at the morula stage of human embryonic development?
(c) Name and state the function of the middle wall of the human uterus.
extractionIssues: Official answer for (a) is a two-column comparison table, flattened row by row

officialAnswer.text:
(a)(1) Leydig cells: Located in the interstitial spaces (connective tissue) surrounding the seminiferous tubules. | Sertoli cells: Located in the seminiferous epithelium within the seminiferous tubules.
(a)(2) Corpus luteum: Secretes progesterone | Placenta: Secretes chorionic gonadotropin, estrogen, progesterone, relaxin, hPL
(b) Without zona pellucida, which prevents adhesion, the morula may prematurely attach to the wall of the Fallopian tube and may lead to ectopic pregnancy.
(c) Myometrium
It brings about powerful contractions of the uterus during parturition.

questions.text:
(a) For artificial hybridisation of pea plants, fresh pollens from the anther can be used, whereas preserved pollens are mandatory for wheat hybridisation. Why?
(b) Study the table below and answer the following questions:
Fruit | Fruit and Seed formation
X | Cells of the integument develop into an embryo
Y | Ovary develops into seedless fruit by the application of phytohormones
Z | Peduncle contributes to fruit formation
(1) Which of these fruits exhibits polyembryony? Will its embryos exhibit genetic variation? Justify your answer with a reason.
(2) Identify the fruit type of ‘Y’.

officialAnswer.text:
(a) Pea plant belongs to the Leguminosae family whose pollen can remain viable for several months and years. But pollens of wheat remain viable for only 30 minutes.
(b)(1) Fruit X
It will not exhibit genetic variation.
This is so because the embryo develops from the cells of the integument by mitosis and not by fertilisation.
(b)(2) ‘Y’ is a parthenocarpic fruit.

questions.text:
The graph provided below shows a classic predator-prey interaction, with predator population peaks lagging slightly behind prey population peaks.
(a) Assume that a sudden viral disease wipes out 80% of the predator population at Year 6 (instead of the natural decline shown in the graph). Construct a new version of the above graph from Year 6 onward showing both the prey and predator curves.
(b) Interpret the population dynamics responsible for changes in the constructed graph.
extractionIssues: Official answer for (a) is a hand-drawn continuation of the graph; not reproduced in text layer (only fragmented axis/legend text, e.g. 'Predator Population', 'Prey Population', was extracted)

officialAnswer.text:
(b) • The abundant prey provides more food, allowing the predator population to recover gradually over the following years.
• As predators recover, the prey population begins to decline, approaching a new ecological balance.

figures.alt: Line graph of prey population (solid line, circle markers, left axis 0 to 250) and predator population (dashed line, square markers, right axis 0 to 45) against year 1 to 12

questions.text:
A population of 100 beetles is introduced into an environment with a carrying capacity of 500. The intrinsic rate of natural increase for this beetle species is 0·2 per year.
(a) Calculate the change in population size after the first year.
(b) Using the given data, draw a population growth curve showing how the beetle population changes with time as it approaches the carrying capacity. Label the following in the graph.
• Initial population
• Carrying capacity
• Phase of maximum growth rate
• Stationary phase
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (logistic growth equation dN/dt = rN((K-N)/K), stacked in the PDF); check against the PDF
Official answer for (b) includes a hand-drawn population growth curve graph not reproduced in text layer; only the label 'Phase of maximum growth (N=k/2)' was captured

officialAnswer.text:
(a) dN/dt = rN((K − N)/K)
dN/dt = 0.2 × 100 × ((500 − 100)/500)
dN/dt = 20 × 0.8 = 16
(b) Phase of maximum growth (N=k/2)
